# az-tf-mlz-management

The management resources of a Fortytwo managed landing zone (MLZ), in AzAPI: a Log Analytics workspace,
the three data collection rules the Azure landing zone (ALZ) policies take, and the Azure Monitor Agent's
user-assigned identity. It replaces `avm-ptn-alz-management` and AVM's Log Analytics module.

```hcl
module "management" {
  source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-management.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"

  name      = "law-management"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/<subscription>/resourceGroups/rg-management"
  location  = "swedencentral"
  data_collection_rules = {
    change_tracking = { name = "dcr-change-tracking" }
    vm_insights     = { name = "dcr-vm-insights" }
    defender_sql    = { name = "dcr-defender-sql" }
  }
  user_assigned_identity = { name = "id-ama" }
  lock                   = { kind = "CanNotDelete" }
}
```

## What it creates

- **The workspace** (`modules/log_analytics_workspace`), always, on the `PerGB2018` pricing tier: 30 days
  of retention by default, no daily cap, local authentication (shared keys) off, resource-context access
  on, public ingestion and query on. Role assignments and diagnostic settings go on the workspace.
- **The legacy solutions whose tables the rules send to:** `ChangeTracking` with the change tracking rule,
  `SQLAdvancedThreatProtection` and `SQLVulnerabilityAssessment` with the Defender for SQL rule. Azure
  refuses a rule whose destination table does not exist (`InvalidOutputTable`), and a solution adds its
  tables about a minute after it is created, so `retry` retries that error by default.
- **The data collection rules** (`modules/data_collection_rule`), each when named, in the workspace's
  region and sending to it, with the bodies of `avm-ptn-alz-management`: change tracking and inventory for
  Windows and Linux; VM insights performance counters, with processes and dependencies (the Map) only when
  `processes_and_dependencies_enabled` is set; Microsoft Defender for SQL on machines.
- **The identity** (`modules/user_assigned_identity`), when named.
- **The lock** goes on the workspace (which covers its Sentinel onboarding), the rules and the identity.
- **Microsoft Sentinel** (`modules/sentinel_onboarding`), when `sentinel_onboarding` is set: onboarded on
  the workspace. Sentinel bills the data it analyses.
- **Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans** (`modules/defender_plan`), one per entry of `defender_plans`, on
  any subscription: `tier = "Free"` turns a plan off, and removing an entry leaves Azure as it is (a
  subscription's plans always exist). An unset `sub_plan` and unlisted extensions stay as Azure has them. With the ALZ policies, give each plan one owner: this, or
  `Deploy-MDFC-Config-H224`'s `enableAscFor*` parameters.

**Sentinel and the Defender plans are not tested in Azure.** By decision they are released without a
sandbox test (a plan bills every protected resource of a subscription), and the first customer deployment
is their first test. Only their bodies are checked, against the AzAPI provider's schema: Sentinel's by
`azapi_resource` itself, the Defender plans' through a unit-test fixture, because `azapi_update_resource`
does not validate its body.

The outputs give what `avm-ptn-alz`'s `policy_default_values` take: `resource_id`
(`log_analytics_workspace_id`), `data_collection_rule_resource_ids` (`change_tracking`, `vm_insights`,
`defender_sql`) and `user_assigned_identity` (`resource_id`, `name`). That input takes each value as
`jsonencode({ value = ... })`; `examples/default` builds the map.

Not created: the resource group, an automation account and its linked service (Azure Update Manager and
change tracking with the Azure Monitor Agent need none), other legacy solutions (VM insights with the
Azure Monitor Agent needs none, the Map included), Sentinel's data connectors and analytics rules, and
Defender for Cloud's security contacts and continuous export (the ALZ policies set those). Associations between machines
and the rules are left to the ALZ policies.

## Behaviour to know

- **Soft delete.** A deleted workspace is kept for 14 days and its name stays reserved; creating a
  workspace with the same name, resource group and region in that time recovers it with its data.
  `permanently_delete_on_destroy = true` deletes it permanently instead (development and tests).
- **ALZ denies deleting the identity** (`DenyAction-DeleteUAMIAMA`): where that policy is assigned,
  removing or renaming `user_assigned_identity` fails until the policy is exempted.
- **A `ReadOnly` lock** blocks updates of the locked resources themselves: remove it before changing them.
- Every submodule can be called alone, for example a workload's own data collection rule:
  `source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-management.git//modules/data_collection_rule?ref=vX.Y.Z"`.

## Optional Inputs

The following input variables are optional (have default values):

### <a name="input_daily_quota_gb"></a> [daily\_quota\_gb](#input\_daily\_quota\_gb)

Description: (Optional) Daily ingestion cap in GB. Ingestion stops for the rest of the day once it is reached. Defaults to `null`, no cap.

Type: `number`

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_data_collection_rules"></a> [data\_collection\_rules](#input\_data\_collection\_rules)

Description: The data collection rules the Azure landing zone (ALZ) policies take, each created when named. They send to  
the workspace and are created in its region. Defaults to none.

- `change_tracking` - (Optional) Change tracking and inventory for Windows and Linux (`Deploy-VM-ChangeTrack` and related policies).
  - `name` - Name of the rule.
- `vm_insights` - (Optional) VM insights performance counters (`Deploy-VM-Monitoring` and related policies).
  - `name` - Name of the rule.
  - `processes_and_dependencies_enabled` - (Optional) Also collect processes and dependencies for the VM insights Map, through the Dependency agent. Defaults to `false`, as VM insights does, to save ingestion cost.
- `defender_sql` - (Optional) Microsoft Defender for SQL on machines (`Deploy-MDFC-DefSQL-AMA`).
  - `name` - Name of the rule.
  - `sql_queries_collection_enabled` - (Optional) Collect SQL queries for security research. Defaults to `false`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    change_tracking = optional(object({
      name = string
    }))
    vm_insights = optional(object({
      name                               = string
      processes_and_dependencies_enabled = optional(bool, false)
    }))
    defender_sql = optional(object({
      name                           = string
      sql_queries_collection_enabled = optional(bool, false)
    }))
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_defender_plans"></a> [defender\_plans](#input\_defender\_plans)

Description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans, keyed by a stable name of your choice, each on one subscription. A  
subscription's plans always exist: `tier = "Free"` turns one off, and removing an entry leaves Azure as it  
is (turn it off first). A Standard plan bills every protected resource in its subscription. With the Azure  
landing zone policies, give each plan one owner: this, or `Deploy-MDFC-Config-H224`'s `enableAscFor*`.  
Not tested in Azure: released without a sandbox test by decision, its first test is the first customer  
deployment. Defaults to none.

- `subscription_id` - Resource ID of the subscription, `/subscriptions/<id>`.
- `plan` - Defender plan (pricing) name, for example `VirtualMachines`, `SqlServers`, `StorageAccounts`, `KeyVaults`, `Containers`, `CloudPosture`.
- `tier` - (Optional) `Standard` (on, default) or `Free` (off).
- `sub_plan` - (Optional) Sub-plan of a Standard plan, for example `P1` or `P2` for `VirtualMachines`. Unset, Azure's sub-plan stands.
- `extensions` - (Optional) Extensions of the plan, keyed by extension name, each `{ enabled, additional_properties }`. Only the listed ones are managed; the others, and one removed from the map, stay as Azure has them.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    subscription_id = string
    plan            = string
    tier            = optional(string, "Standard")
    sub_plan        = optional(string)
    extensions = optional(map(object({
      enabled               = bool
      additional_properties = optional(map(string))
    })), {})
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on the Log Analytics workspace. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name = optional(string, null)
    logs = optional(set(object({
      category       = optional(string, null)
      category_group = optional(string, null)
      enabled        = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    metrics = optional(set(object({
      category = optional(string, null)
      enabled  = optional(bool, true)
      retention_policy = optional(object({
        days    = optional(number, 0)
        enabled = optional(bool, false)
      }), {})
    })), [])
    log_analytics_destination_type           = optional(string, "Dedicated")
    workspace_resource_id                    = optional(string, null)
    storage_account_resource_id              = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    event_hub_name                           = optional(string, null)
    marketplace_partner_resource_id          = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_ignore_body_changes"></a> [ignore\_body\_changes](#input\_ignore\_body\_changes)

Description: Paths in each resource's `body` whose changes the AzAPI provider ignores. Prefer Terraform's `lifecycle.ignore_changes` when the paths are static; use this variable when the paths must be derived from variables or other non-static values.

Paths use dot notation, for example `properties.retentionInDays`. Individual list items cannot be targeted; ignore the whole list property instead. Configuration changes at an ignored path are **not** sent to Azure until that path is removed from the list. Changes take effect only after an apply, because the value is held in provider-private state.

- `operationalinsights_workspaces` - Slot for `modules/log_analytics_workspace`: its `operationalinsights_workspaces`, `authorization_locks`, `authorization_role_assignments`, `insights_diagnostic_settings`, `operationsmanagement_solutions`, and its slot for `modules/sentinel_onboarding` (`securityinsights_onboarding_states`). Defender plans have none: they are updated in place (`azapi_update_resource`), which has no `ignore_body_changes`.
- `insights_data_collection_rules` - Slot for `modules/data_collection_rule`, applied to every rule: its `insights_data_collection_rules`, `authorization_locks`, `authorization_role_assignments` and `insights_diagnostic_settings`.
- `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities` - Slot for `modules/user_assigned_identity`: its `managedidentity_user_assigned_identities`, `authorization_locks` and `authorization_role_assignments`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    operationalinsights_workspaces = optional(object({
      operationalinsights_workspaces = optional(list(string), [])
      authorization_locks            = optional(list(string), [])
      authorization_role_assignments = optional(list(string), [])
      insights_diagnostic_settings   = optional(list(string), [])
      operationsmanagement_solutions = optional(list(string), [])
      securityinsights_onboarding_states = optional(object({
        securityinsights_onboarding_states = optional(list(string), [])
      }), {})
    }), {})
    insights_data_collection_rules = optional(object({
      insights_data_collection_rules = optional(list(string), [])
      authorization_locks            = optional(list(string), [])
      authorization_role_assignments = optional(list(string), [])
      insights_diagnostic_settings   = optional(list(string), [])
    }), {})
    managedidentity_user_assigned_identities = optional(object({

      authorization_role_assignments           = optional(list(string), [])
    }), {})
  })
```

### <a name="input_lock"></a> [lock](#input\_lock)

Description: A lock on the resources the module creates in the resource group: the workspace (which covers its Sentinel onboarding), the data collection rules and the identity. The ALZ policies refer to all of them. Defender plans are not locked: a lock at subscription scope would lock the subscription. The following properties can be specified:

- `kind` - (Required) The type of lock. Possible values are `\"CanNotDelete\"` and `\"ReadOnly\"`.
- `name` - (Optional) The name of the lock. If not specified, a name will be generated based on the `kind` value. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `notes` - (Optional) Notes about the lock. This value maps to `Microsoft.Authorization/locks.properties.notes`.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    kind  = string
    name  = optional(string, null)
    notes = optional(string, null)
  })
```

Default: `null`

### <a name="input_permanently_delete_on_destroy"></a> [permanently\_delete\_on\_destroy](#input\_permanently\_delete\_on\_destroy)

Description: Whether destroying the workspace deletes it permanently. Defaults to `false`: Azure keeps a deleted workspace and its data recoverable for 14 days and reserves its name, and creating a workspace with the same name, resource group and region in that time recovers it.

Type: `bool`

Default: `false`

### <a name="input_public_network_access_for_ingestion"></a> [public\_network\_access\_for\_ingestion](#input\_public\_network\_access\_for\_ingestion)

Description: Whether the workspace accepts ingestion over public networks: `Enabled` (default) or `Disabled` (only through an Azure Monitor Private Link Scope).

### <a name="input_resource_permissions_enabled"></a> [resource\_permissions\_enabled](#input\_resource\_permissions\_enabled)

### <a name="input_retention_in_days"></a> [retention\_in\_days](#input\_retention\_in\_days)

### <a name="input_retry"></a> [retry](#input\_retry)

Description: Retry configuration applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module and its submodules. Defaults retry `InvalidOutputTable`, which Azure returns for a data collection rule whose destination table does not exist yet: a solution adds its tables about a minute after it is created (sandbox, 2026-10-28). Any field can be overridden.

- `error_message_regex`  - (Optional) A list of regex patterns matching error messages that trigger a retry. Defaults to `["InvalidOutputTable"]`.
- `interval_seconds`     - (Optional) Initial interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `30`.
- `max_interval_seconds` - (Optional) Maximum interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `300`.

See <https://registry.terraform.io/providers/Azure/azapi/latest/docs/resources/resource#retry> for full semantics.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    error_message_regex  = optional(list(string), ["InvalidOutputTable"])
    interval_seconds     = optional(number, 30)
    max_interval_seconds = optional(number, 300)
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the Log Analytics workspace. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

## Outputs

The following outputs are exported:

### <a name="output_data_collection_rule_resource_ids"></a> [data\_collection\_rule\_resource\_ids](#output\_data\_collection\_rule\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the data collection rules the module created, by kind: `change_tracking`, `vm_insights`, `defender_sql`. For `avm-ptn-alz`'s `policy_default_values`: `ama_change_tracking_data_collection_rule_id`, `ama_vm_insights_data_collection_rule_id` and `ama_mdfc_sql_data_collection_rule_id`.

### <a name="output_defender_plan_resource_ids"></a> [defender\_plan\_resource\_ids](#output\_defender\_plan\_resource\_ids)

Description: Resource IDs of the Defender plans the module sets, by key of `defender_plans`.

### <a name="output_name"></a> [name](#output\_name)

Description: Name of the Log Analytics workspace.

### <a name="output_resource_id"></a> [resource\_id](#output\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the Log Analytics workspace (`log_analytics_workspace_id` in `avm-ptn-alz`'s `policy_default_values`).

### <a name="output_sentinel_onboarding_resource_id"></a> [sentinel\_onboarding\_resource\_id](#output\_sentinel\_onboarding\_resource\_id)

Description: Resource ID of the workspace's Microsoft Sentinel onboarding state; null when Sentinel is not onboarded.

### <a name="output_user_assigned_identity"></a> [user\_assigned\_identity](#output\_user\_assigned\_identity)

Description: The Azure Monitor Agent's user-assigned identity: `resource_id`, `name`, `principal_id` and `client_id`; null when none was created. For `avm-ptn-alz`'s `policy_default_values`: `ama_user_assigned_managed_identity_id` and `ama_user_assigned_managed_identity_name`.

### <a name="output_workspace_id"></a> [workspace\_id](#output\_workspace\_id)

Description: Workspace (customer) ID of the Log Analytics workspace, a GUID.

## Development

Tools: Terraform 1.17.0, TFLint 0.65.0, terraform-docs 0.24.0 (the versions CI uses).

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Format, validate, lint, unit tests, README drift (what CI runs) | `scripts/check.sh` |
| Format the code and regenerate the READMEs first | `scripts/check.sh --fix` |
| Integration tests in Azure | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/integration.sh [dir ...]` |
| Examples: apply, plan again (must be empty), destroy | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/e2e.sh [examples/<name> ...]` |

`README.md` files are generated from `_header.md`, the code and `_footer.md`; do not edit them by hand.

## Versions and releases

Every release is a SemVer tag `vX.Y.Z`; tags never move, and `main` is never consumed. Pin a release:

```hcl
source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/<repository>.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
```

Pull requests are squash-merged, and their titles follow Conventional Commits, which set the next
version: `fix:` a patch, `feat:` a minor (a patch before 1.0.0), `feat!:` or `fix!:` a major (a minor
before 1.0.0). `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:` and `refactor:` release nothing. release-please keeps a
release pull request open; merging it writes `CHANGELOG.md`, the tag and the GitHub release.
